lines.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!
I know that you are pregnant!
It does not matter who told me this.
The main thing is that I am here.
I am ready to be the father of this child.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'a minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Катя, можно тебя на пару минут?
examples.trans: Katya, can I have you for a couple of minutes?

examples.text: Дайте нам пару минут, это очень важно.
examples.trans: Give us a couple of minutes, this is very important.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?

examples.text: Слушай, Эля, ты думаешь, я ничего не понимаю?
examples.trans: Listen, Elya, do you think I understand nothing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'drink', paired with 'выпить'.

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!
I'm drinking tea.
He doesn't drink.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'greenhorn / rookie' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!

examples.text: Огузок, ты официально принят в штат нашего ресторана!
examples.trans: Rump, you are officially hired onto our restaurant staff!
Runt, are you still standing here?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'returned', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.trans: I'll be back soon.
He came back home.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It turns out we are friends in misfortune.
Katya and I broke up.
We are exchanging curious facts, after all.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to talk!
I need to know the truth.

examples.text: Ему нужна мама для его дочки.
examples.trans: He needs a mother for his daughter.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: We need to talk!
Go to our place, we will talk tonight.
I need to talk with the doctor.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know'.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!

examples.text: Я узнала о тебе много нового.
examples.trans: I learned a lot of new things about you.

examples.text: Даже не знаешь человека и защищаешь его.
examples.trans: You do not even know the man and you defend him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

examples.text: Тем более, что ты уже начал.
examples.trans: Especially since you have already started.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?
In a divorce, two people are always at fault.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pregnant').

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!

examples.text: Моя бывшая беременна, говорит, что не от меня.
examples.trans: My ex is pregnant and says it is not mine.
You're not pregnant at all!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Who told you?

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: А меня Виктория просила ничего не говорить.
examples.trans: And Victoria asked me not to say anything.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'said', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Who told you?

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Обо мне ведь ничего не рассказал.
examples.trans: After all, you told her nothing about me.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important, mattering').

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.
Forgive me, this is very important.
This is important for your career.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the main thing').

examples.trans: The main thing is that I am here.
The main thing is, don't worry.
This is the main street.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is that I am here.
What does that have to do with this?
Lena, what are we doing here?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ready').

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
I'm ready!
Lunch is ready.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be'.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
That simply cannot be!
I have a toy car.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'father' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он хотел в чём-то мне признаться.
examples.trans: He wanted to confess something to me.
Kostya wanted to cover for me.
And who is the father?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child / baby' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
This is not your child.

examples.text: Ну чей это ребёнок, если не твой?
examples.trans: Well whose child is it, if not yours?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How noble.
As a subordinate.

examples.text: Это какую правду Кате не расскажешь?
examples.trans: What truth can you not tell Katya?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: How noble.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно благородно и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite noble and calmly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'слабиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'relax', paired with 'расслабляться'.

examples.trans: Vanya, relax.
I want to relax.

examples.text: Ваня, расслабься. В этот раз без обмана.
examples.trans: Vanya, relax. This time there's no trick.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This is not your child.

examples.text: Ну чей это ребёнок, если не твой?
examples.trans: Well whose child is it, if not yours?

examples.text: Убедиться в том, что ребёнок твой, очень просто.
examples.trans: Making sure that the child is yours is very simple.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: That simply cannot be!
You are simply jealous of me.

examples.text: Убедиться в том, что ребёнок твой, очень просто.
examples.trans: Making sure that the child is yours is very simple.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That simply cannot be!
Maybe she was joking?

examples.text: А может, это ребёнок не от меня, правда?
examples.trans: Maybe this child really is not mine?
